messages:
maya: quick postmortem-followup from the autoscale surge last week — consolidating owners and next steps. i sketched a closure plan below, please ✅ or suggest edits.

maya: ACTIONS: 
1) quota safety margin -> set default project quota buffer to 12% (owner: alex) — aim: reduce sudden OOM-driven evictions
2) scheduler tuning -> relax preemption backoff + adjust packing threshold from 0.7 -> 0.65 (owner: sam)
3) headroom sim -> run 48h synthetic soak sim against peak mix to validate buffer (owner: jin)
4) canary & rollback -> add a 6h canary window + automated fallback to smaller model variant (owner: alex + ops-bot)
5) runbook & alerting -> add new alert for quota-exhaustion rate > 3/min and link remediation steps (owner: maya)

maya: timeline: propose PRs/tests by EOW (Fri), canary next Tue, full rollout after successful canary (~+7d).

alex: reading. +1 on 12% buffer. i can own the quota bake and API guardrails.

sam: scheduler change sounds fine but want to run a quick perf sweep — lowering packing threshold may increase infra cost. i'll add a perf matrix.

jin: i can run the headroom sim. need the workload traces — maya can you drop the S3 path? also I'll containerize the sim and log to /sim-results.

maya: s3://redwood-incidents/autoscale/2026-03-headroom-traces.tar.gz — contains 7 days of peak traces and an anonymized user workload mix. jin: ping when you start so we can watch.

jin: started a small job on dev-cluster now. ps: using the new batching profile, results look promising at 25% lower latency under pressure, will post a short table when done.

ops-bot: deploy-triggered: quota-batch-pr -> created by alex (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4281)

alex: PR open ^, includes API guard that enforces project_quota_min = max(requested, baseline*1.12). unit tests added. request review from infra-owners.

sam: created scheduler perf sweep issue: https://go.redwood/scheduler-perf-632 
params: packing_thresholds=[0.6,0.65,0.7], preempt_backoff_ms=[200,500,1000], run_length=2h each. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility.

maya: good. can we add an explicit owner for followup status checks? i propose weekly 15-min sync for first 3 weeks, owner rotates: week1 alex, week2 sam, week3 jin.

alex: i'm fine week1. i'll monitor canary metrics: eviction_rate, p90_latency, model_throughput, quota_headroom_pct.

sam: if perf sweep shows cost spike >8% at 0.65, we should consider an adaptive packing rule instead of static change. adding note to issue.

jin: sim complete on dev — uploading logs to /sim-results/3287654321.tar.gz. quick takeaway: 12% quota buffer reduced eviction tail by ~78%, but packing @0.65 raised 99th latency on heavy tails by ~4%. more analysis incoming.

maya: great. next steps: alex -> merge quota PR after +2 reviewer approvals; sam -> finish perf sweep and post recommendations; jin -> post full sim report and recommend canary config; maya -> update runbook and create the canary dashboard.

alex: will aim to merge today pending reviews.

sam: perf sweep scheduled to finish tomorrow morning.

jin: report uploaded: https://drive.redwood/sim-reports/3287654321-summary.pdf — tl;dr: proceed with canary but use adaptive packing at 0.66 as compromise.

maya: noted. changing canary plan: use adaptive packing=0.66, canary window 6h, abort criteria: eviction_rate > 1/min OR p99 latency uplift >10% OR quota_headroom_pct < 6%.

ops-bot: canary-runner: started canary on cluster prod-canary-3 (id: cr-3287654321)

alex: watching canary dashboards. no evictions so far in first 90m. p99 +2% — within threshold.

sam: will stand by in case preemption noise spikes.

maya: if canary completes clean, assign closure ticket and add to postmortem as "actions completed". is everyone OK with that?

alex: OK from me.

sam: ok.

jin: ok, thanks.

maya: thanks all — i'll post final closure + updated runbook link here once canary finishes. :party:
